calculators.title_native: Singapore Take-Home Pay & CPF Contribution Calculator (IRAS Income Tax & CPF OW/AW Ceiling 2025/2026)
calculators.title_en: Singapore Take-Home Pay & CPF Contribution Calculator (IRAS Income Tax & CPF OW/AW Ceiling 2025/2026)
calculators.description_native: Calculate your net monthly take-home pay, IRAS personal income tax, and mandatory employee & employer CPF contributions under the updated 2024-2026 OW salary ceiling ($6,800 to $8,000) and age-tiered contribution rates for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents (PR Year 1, 2, and 3+).

inputs.name: srs_contribution
inputs.label_native: Annual Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS) Voluntary Contribution (S$)

inputs.name: other_tax_reliefs
inputs.label_native: Other Personal Tax Reliefs (CPF Top-Up, NSman, Child Relief) (S$)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Ordinary Wages (OW) Monthly CPF Ceiling: $6,800/mo (2024), $7,400/mo (2025), $8,000/mo (2026). OW Subject to CPF = Min(Gross Monthly Salary, OW Ceiling).
2. Additional Wages (AW) Annual CPF Ceiling: $102,000 - Total Annual OW subject to CPF. AW Subject to CPF = Min(Annual Bonus, AW Ceiling).
3. Full CPF Rates (Citizens & PR 3rd Year+):
   - Age <= 55: Employee 20%, Employer 17% (Total 37%). Max Employee CPF OW cap = $1,480/mo (2025).
   - Age > 55 to 60: Employee 17%, Employer 15.5% (Total 32.5%).
   - Age > 60 to 65: Employee 12.5%, Employer 12% (Total 24.5%).
   - Age > 65 to 70: Employee 7.5%, Employer 9% (Total 16.5%).
   - Age > 70: Employee 5%, Employer 7.5% (Total 12.5%).
4. Graduated PR Rates (Yr 1 Standard: Employee 5% / Employer 4%; Yr 2 Standard: Employee 15% / Employer 9%).
5. Net Monthly Take-Home Pay = Gross Monthly Salary - Monthly Employee CPF.
6. Annual Chargeable Income = Gross Annual Income (OW * 12 + AW) - Employee CPF Deductions - SRS Relief (Max $15,300 SC/PR, $35,700 Foreigner) - Earned Income Relief ($1,000-$8,000) - Other Reliefs (Subject to $80,000 total relief cap).
7. IRAS Personal Income Tax (YA 2024/2025): First $20k (0%), next $10k (2%), next $10k (3.5%), next $40k (7%), next $40k (11.5%), next $40k (15%), next $40k (18%), next $40k (19%), next $40k (20%), next $40k (21%), next $180k (22%), next $500k (23%), >$1M (24%). Subtract 50% Personal Income Tax Rebate (capped at $200).

calculators.title_native: Singapore Property Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) & ABSD Tax Calculator
calculators.title_en: Singapore Property Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) & ABSD Tax Calculator
calculators.description_native: Calculate progressive Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) for residential and non-residential property purchases in Singapore across Singapore Citizens, PRs, Foreigners, Entities, and joint buyers.

inputs.name: property_type
options: Residential Property (HDB / Executive Condo / Private Condo / Landed)

inputs.name: buyer_profile
inputs.label_native: Buyer Residency Status & Owned Property Count

inputs.name: is_joint_purchase_sc_spr
inputs.label_native: Joint Matrimonial Purchase (SC + SPR Spouse 1st Property)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Residential Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) Tiers:
   - First S$180,000: 1%
   - Next S$180,000 (S$180k - S$360k): 2%
   - Next S$640,000 (S$360k - S$1.0M): 3%
   - Next S$500,000 (S$1.0M - S$1.5M): 4%
   - Next S$1,500,000 (S$1.5M - S$3.0M): 5%
   - Portion exceeding S$3,000,000: 6%
2. Non-Residential BSD Tiers:
   - First S$180k (1%), Next S$180k (2%), Next S$640k (3%), Next S$500k (4%), Portion > S$1.5M (5%).
3. Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) Rates (Residential):
   - Singapore Citizen (SC): 1st property (0%), 2nd property (20%), 3rd+ (30%).
   - Singapore PR (SPR): 1st property (5%), 2nd property (30%), 3rd+ (35%).
   - Foreigner: 60% flat across all residential purchases.
   - Entities / Corporate: 65% flat.
   - Housing Developers: 35% + 5% non-remittable.
4. Joint SC + SPR married couples purchasing their 1st residential property qualify for ABSD remission (0%).
5. Total Property Stamp Duty = BSD + ABSD.

calculators.title_native: Singapore Company Corporate Income Tax & Startup Tax Exemption (SUTE) Calculator
calculators.title_en: Singapore Company Corporate Income Tax & Startup Tax Exemption (SUTE) Calculator
search_terms_native: sute vs pte exemption calculator iras
calculators.description_native: Calculate your Singapore Private Limited (Pte Ltd) company tax liability, comparing Startup Tax Exemption (SUTE) for the first 3 YAs against Partial Tax Exemption (PTE), plus Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rebates.

inputs.name: company_eligibility
options: SUTE - Qualifying New Startup Company (First 3 Consecutive YAs)
PTE - Partial Tax Exemption (Normal / Established Company)

inputs.name: ya_year
options: YA 2025 (50% CIT Rebate capped at $40,000 + Cash Payout)

inputs.name: local_employees_count
inputs.label_native: Local Employees Hired (Singaporeans/PRs receiving CPF in previous year)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Singapore Flat Corporate Tax Rate: 17% on Net Chargeable Income.
2. Startup Tax Exemption (SUTE) Scheme (First 3 YAs for eligible new startups):
   - 75% exemption on first S$100,000 chargeable income (effective tax rate 4.25%). Max exempt = S$75,000.
   - 50% exemption on next S$100,000 chargeable income (effective tax rate 8.5%). Max exempt = S$50,000.
   - Maximum total SUTE exemption = S$125,000 per year.
3. Partial Tax Exemption (PTE) Scheme (All other companies & post-3rd YA startups):
   - 75% exemption on first S$10,000 chargeable income (effective tax rate 4.25%). Max exempt = S$7,500.
   - 50% exemption on next S$190,000 chargeable income (effective tax rate 8.5%). Max exempt = S$95,000.
   - Maximum total PTE exemption = S$102,500 per year.
4. Gross Corporate Tax = (Chargeable Income - Exempt Income) * 17%.
5. Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Rebate: 50% of Gross Corporate Tax, capped at S$40,000. Companies employing at least 1 local employee receive a minimum S$2,000 CIT Rebate Cash Payout.
6. Net Corporate Tax Payable = Max(0, Gross Corporate Tax - CIT Rebate).
7. Single-Tier Dividend System: Dividends distributed to shareholders out of after-tax corporate profits are 100% tax-free.

calculators.title_native: Singapore Freelancer & Self-Employed Medisave & Income Tax Calculator
calculators.title_en: Singapore Freelancer & Self-Employed Medisave & Income Tax Calculator
search_terms_native: commission agent fixed expense ratio tax sg
calculators.description_native: Calculate compulsory CPF Medisave contributions and IRAS personal income tax for Singapore self-employed persons, sole proprietors, and freelancers, including the 15% fixed expense ratio option.

inputs.name: gross_trade_income
inputs.label_native: Gross Trade Revenue / Total Client Invoices (S$)

inputs.name: deduction_method
options: 15% Prescribed Fixed Expense Ratio (Commission agents / Drivers)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Net Trade Income (NTI) = Gross Trade Revenue - Max(Actual Allowable Expenses, Gross Revenue * 15% if using prescribed ratio).
2. Compulsory Medisave Requirement: Self-Employed Persons (SEPs) earning NTI > S$6,000/year must contribute to CPF Medisave.
3. Medisave Contribution Rates (Tiered by NTI level, capped at Medisave ceiling NTI S$72,000):
   - Age <35: 4% to 8% of NTI (Max S$5,760/yr).
   - Age 35-44: 4.5% to 9.5% of NTI (Max S$6,840/yr).
   - Age 45-49: 5% to 10% of NTI (Max S$7,200/yr).
   - Age 50+: 5.5% to 10.5% of NTI (Max S$7,560/yr).
4. Medisave Tax Relief: Mandatory Medisave contributions made by self-employed individuals are 100% tax-deductible against Personal Income Tax.
5. Total Taxable Income = NTI + Other Employment Income - Medisave Contribution - Voluntary SRS (max $15,300 SC/PR) - Earned Income Relief ($1,000-$8,000).
6. IRAS Personal Income Tax is computed via progressive tax bands (0% to 24%) minus 50% Personal Income Tax Rebate (capped at $200).

calculators.title_native: Singapore Tenancy Agreement Stamp Duty & Landlord Rental Income Tax Calculator
calculators.title_en: Singapore Tenancy Agreement Stamp Duty & Landlord Rental Income Tax Calculator
search_terms_native: net rental income tax calculator sg
calculators.description_native: Calculate IRAS tenancy agreement stamp duty for tenants/landlords and net taxable rental income for property owners using actual expenses vs the 15% simplified expense ratio.

inputs.name: monthly_rent
inputs.label_native: Gross Monthly Rent (including furniture & maintenance fees) (S$)

inputs.name: landlord_expense_option
options: 15% Deemed Rental Expense Ratio + Mortgage Loan Interest
Actual Allowable Rental Expenses (Repairs, Agent Fees, Property Tax, Mortgage Interest)

inputs.name: actual_rental_expenses
inputs.label_native: Actual Annual Operating Expenses (excl. Mortgage Interest) (S$)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Average Annual Rent (AAV) = (Gross Monthly Rent * Lease Duration Months + Advance Premium) / (Lease Duration Months / 12).
2. IRAS Tenancy Stamp Duty:
   - For lease duration <= 4 years (<= 48 months): 0.4% of total rent payable across the full lease period.
   - For lease duration > 4 years (> 48 months): 0.4% of 4 x AAV (equivalent to 1.6% of AAV).
   - If advance premium paid: Additional 0.4% tax on the premium amount.
3. Landlord Gross Annual Rental Income = Monthly Rent * 12.
4. Landlord Taxable Net Rental Income:
   - Deemed Expense Option: Net Rent = Gross Annual Rent - (Gross Annual Rent * 15%) - Annual Mortgage Interest.
   - Actual Expense Option: Net Rent = Gross Annual Rent - Actual Allowable Expenses - Annual Mortgage Interest.
5. Net Rental Income is added to personal income tax computation (taxed at progressive rates 0% to 24%) or corporate tax computation (taxed at 17%).
